subject.title: Durable Core PR 5/6: add operation-scoped execution recovery

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this durable execution-and-recovery control plane, including its shared SQLite state and authority-mode behavior, as a core product boundary?
rationale: The implementation adds a new cross-owner runtime model, persistent state, recovery policy, and configuration surface; this is an architecture and compatibility choice rather than a mechanical correctness question.

options.title: Sponsor the durable core
options.body: Approve the core direction and require explicit migration, rollback, and operator-behavior evidence before merging the stacked series.

options.title: Narrow to owner-specific recovery
options.body: Keep only recovery seams that existing owners can use without introducing a generic durable execution worker or new core authority mode.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Pause the stack until a maintainer-approved architecture proposal defines ownership, upgrade guarantees, and supported operating modes.

recommendation.title: Narrow to owner-specific recovery
recommendation.body: Keep only recovery seams that existing owners can use without introducing a generic durable execution worker or new core authority mode.

likelyOwner.reason: The available evidence connects this contributor to the full proposed durable-runtime stack, although current-main feature ownership remains unverified.
